Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 63, verse 1–4:

Surat al-Munafiqun is Madani (revealed in Medina). [[Reported by Ibn al-Durays, al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The surah of the hypocrites was revealed in Medina." Ibn Mardawayh also reported the same from Ibn al-Zubayr. See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/170.]] In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

* *

﴿When the hypocrites come to you﴾ meaning 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul and his companions, ﴿they say, "We testify that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah." And Allah knows that you are indeed His Messenger, and Allah testifies that the hypocrites are indeed liars﴾, because they concealed the opposite of what they displayed.

﴿They take their oaths as a shield﴾ a cover, ﴿and thus they bar [others] from the way of Allah﴾ they prevented people from jihad and from believing in Muhammad (ﷺ).

﴿Indeed, evil is what they used to do.﴾ ﴿That is because they believed⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿—﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿—they affirmed with the tongue when they saw the believers﴾, ﴿then they disbelieved﴾ when they were alone with the polytheists, ﴿so a seal was set upon their hearts﴾ with disbelief, ﴿and so they do not understand﴾ faith.

﴿When you see them, their bodies impress you﴾ meaning that they have bodies and appearances [that are pleasing], ﴿and if they speak, you listen to their speech﴾ so you think it is true. Ibn 'Abbas said: 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy was tall, eloquent and sharp-tongued; when he spoke, the Prophet (ﷺ) would listen to his speech.

﴿As if they were propped-up pieces of wood﴾ figures without spirits and bodies without minds. Abu 'Amr and al-Kisa'i read "khushb" with a sukun on the shin, while the rest read it with a damma.

﴿Propped up (musannadah)﴾ leaning against a wall, from their saying: "asnadtu al-shay'" when I inclined it. The doubled form indicates intensity. He meant that they are not trees that bear fruit, but rather pieces of wood propped against a wall. ﴿They think every cry is against them﴾ that is, they do not hear any sound in the army, whether a caller calls out or an animal escapes or a lost animal is announced, except that they think—out of their cowardice and bad assumptions—that it is aimed at them, and they think that they have been overtaken, because of the terror in their hearts.

It has also been said: that is because they are in dread lest Allah send down a matter concerning them that exposes their secrets and makes their blood lawful. Then He said: ﴿They are the enemy﴾, and this is an inceptive clause with its predicate, ﴿so beware of them﴾ and do not trust them. ﴿May Allah destroy them﴾ may Allah curse them, ﴿how are they turned away?﴾ how are they diverted from the truth?

﴿When it is said to them, "Come, so that the Messenger of Allah may ask forgiveness for you," they turn their heads﴾: i.e., they turn aside and avert their faces, out of aversion to seeking forgiveness.

Nafi' and Ya'qub read "لَوُوا" (*lawwaw*) with a light (*takhfif*) doubling, while the others read it with emphasis (*tashdid*), as "لَوَّوْا" (*lawwaw*), because they did this repeatedly, time after time.

﴿And you see them turning away﴾: they turn away from what they are called to, ﴿while they are arrogant﴾: proud, disdaining the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asking forgiveness for them.

﴿It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them, O Muhammad, or do not ask forgiveness for them; Allah will never forgive them. Indeed, Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people﴾. Muhammad ibn Ishaq and others, from a group of the scholars of the biographies (*ahl al-siyar*), mentioned that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ received word that the Banu al-Mustaliq were gathering to fight him, and their leader was al-Harith ibn Abi Dirar, the father of [Juwayrah]^[In the two manuscripts it is (Juwayrah), and in others (Juwayriyah).], the wife of the Prophet ﷺ. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard of them, he set out toward them until he met them at one of their watering places called al-Muraysi', on the side of Qudayd toward the coast. The people clashed and fought, and Allah defeated the Banu al-Mustaliq; some of them were killed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took their children, their women and their property, and Allah granted them as spoils [to him]^[In "b" it is "عليه" (upon him).]. While the people were at that water, the arrivals of people came, and with Umar ibn al-Khattab was a hired man of his from the Banu Ghifar, called Jahjah ibn Sa'id al-Ghifari, who was leading his horse. Jahjah and Sinan ibn Wabra al-Juhani, an ally of the Banu Awf ibn al-Khazraj, [over]^[Addition from "b".] the water, got into a struggle and fought. The Juhani shouted, "O company of the Ansar!" and the Ghifari shouted, "O company of the Muhajirun!" A man from the Muhajirun called Jil, who was poor, came to help Jahjah the Ghifari. Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul became angry, and with him was a group of his people, among them Zayd ibn Arqam, a youth still young in years. Ibn Ubayy said, "Did they really do this? They have competed with us and outnumbered us in our own land. By Allah, our situation and theirs is only like what the saying says: 'Fatten your dog and it will eat you.' By Allah, if we return to Medina, the more honored will surely expel the more humble from it." By "the more honored" he meant himself, and by "the more humble" he meant the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then he turned to those of his people who were present and said, "This is what you have done to yourselves: you have let them settle in your land and shared your wealth with them. By Allah, if you withheld from Jil and his people the surplus of food, they would not ride upon your necks, and they would move to some land other than your land. So do not spend on them until they disperse from around Muhammad." Zayd ibn Arqam said, "You are—by Allah—the humble, the lowly, the hated among your people, while Muhammad ﷺ is in the honor of the Most Merciful and in the affection of the Muslims." Abdullah ibn Ubayy said, "Be silent, for I was only joking." He said: Zayd ibn Arqam then walked to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ [and that was]^[Addition from "b".] after he had finished the morning journey, and informed him of the news, while Umar ibn al-Khattab was with him. Umar said, "Let me strike his neck, O Messenger of Allah!" He said, "How, O Umar, if people say that Muhammad kills his companions? Rather, announce the departure," and that was at an hour when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not usually depart; so the people set out.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent for Abdullah ibn Ubayy, and he came to him. He said, "Are you the author of these words that have reached me?" Abdullah said, "By He who sent down the Book to you, I did not say anything of that, and Zayd is lying." Abdullah was a great nobleman among his people. Some of the Ansar who were present among his companions said, "O Messenger of Allah, perhaps the youth was mistaken in his report and did not retain what he said." So the Prophet ﷺ excused him, and blame spread among the Ansar against Zayd, and they denied him. His paternal uncle said to him [and Zayd was with him]^[Addition from "b".]: "You only wanted that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would call you a liar, and the people have come to hate you." Zayd used to ride alongside the Prophet ﷺ, but after that he was ashamed to come near the Prophet ﷺ.

When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went on and proceeded, Usayd ibn Hudayr met him, greeted him with the greeting of prophethood and saluted him. Then he said, "O Messenger of Allah, you have set out at an unusual hour, at which you never used to set out."

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him, "Has it not reached you what your companion Abdullah ibn Ubayy said?" He said, "What did he say?" He said, "He claims that if he returns to Medina, the more honored will expel the more humble from it." Usayd said, "By Allah, you, O Messenger of Allah, will expel him if you wish; he is by Allah the humble one, and you are the mighty one." Then he said, "O Messenger of Allah, be gentle with him, for by Allah Allah has sent you, and his people were arranging beads to crown him, for he thinks that you have taken a kingdom from him."

It reached Abdullah ibn Abdullah ibn Ubayy what his father had done, so he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, it has reached me that you intend to kill Abdullah ibn Ubayy because of what has reached you about him. If you are going to do so, then order me about him, and I will bring you his head. By Allah, the Khazraj know that there was no man in it more dutiful to his parents than I am, and I fear that you will order someone other than me about him, and he will kill him, and my soul will not let me look at the killer of Abdullah ibn Ubayy walking among the people while I do nothing, so I would kill a believer for an unbeliever and enter the Fire."

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Rather, we will be gentle with him and treat his companionship well as long as he remains with us."

They said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ traveled that day until evening, and that night until morning, and the next day until the sun beat down upon them. Then he made the people halt, and they had hardly touched the ground before they fell asleep. He did this only to occupy the people away from the talk that had been yesterday about Abdullah ibn Ubayy.

Then he moved on with the people until he halted at a water in the Hijaz above al-Naqi', called Naq'a. A strong wind blew, which troubled them, and they feared it. The camel of the Prophet ﷺ strayed, and that was at night. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Do not be afraid, for it blew only because of the death of a great one among the great unbelievers, who has died in Medina." It was said, "Who is he?" He said, "Rifa'ah ibn Zayd ibn al-Tabut." A man among the hypocrites said, "How does he claim that he knows the unseen, yet does not know where his camel is? Will the one who brings him revelation not inform him?" Then Gabriel came to him and informed him of the hypocrite's words and of the place of the camel. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ informed his companions of that, and said, "I do not claim that I know the unseen, and I do not know it. But Allah has informed me of the hypocrite's words and of the place of my camel. It is in the ravine, its halter caught on a tree." They went running toward the ravine, and there it was, just as he had said; they brought it back, and that hypocrite believed.

When they reached Medina, they found that Rifa'ah ibn Zayd ibn al-Tabut had died that very day. He had been one of the great men of the Jews and a refuge for the hypocrites. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived at Medina, Zayd ibn Arqam said, "I sat in the house, because of the grief and shame I felt." So Allah the Exalted sent down Surat al-Munafiqun, confirming Zayd and denying Abdullah. When it was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took hold of Zayd's ear and said, "O Zayd, Allah has believed you and fulfilled [the truth of] your ear."

Abdullah ibn Ubayy was near Medina. When he wanted to enter it, his son Abdullah ibn Abdullah came and knelt his camel at the junction of the roads of Medina. When Abdullah ibn Ubayy came, [he said: "Behind you,"]^[Addition from "a" omitted; this is "ساقط من أ" (dropped from manuscript a).] he said, "What is wrong with you, woe to you?" He said, "No, by Allah, you shall never enter it except by the permission of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and today you will know who is the more honored and who is the more humble." Abdullah complained to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ of what his son had done, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent to him, "Let him go until he enters." He said, "As for the command of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, yes." So he entered, and he did not remain more than a few days before he fell ill and died.

They said: When the verse was revealed and the lie of Abdullah ibn Ubayy became clear, it was said to him, "O Abu Hubab, verily severe verses have been revealed about you, so go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he may ask forgiveness for you." He turned his head and said, "You ordered me to believe, and I believed; you ordered me to give the zakat of my wealth, and I have given it. There is nothing left but that I prostrate to Muhammad." So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿When it is said to them, "Come, so that the Messenger of Allah may ask forgiveness for you," they turn their heads﴾ [[Mentioned by Ibn Hisham in al-Sira: 3/302–305 (Dar al-Qalam edition), and al-Tabari: 28/115–117, and Ibn Kathir 4/370–371.]] ... the verse. And it was revealed: ﴿They are the ones who say, "Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse."﴾

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Do not be afraid, for it blew only because of the death of a great one among the great unbelievers, who has died in Medina." It was said, "Who is he?" He said, "Rifa'ah ibn Zayd ibn al-Tabut." A man among the hypocrites said, "How does he claim that he knows the unseen, yet does not know where his camel is? Will the one who brings him revelation not inform him?" Then Gabriel came to him and informed him of the hypocrite's words and of the place of the camel. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ informed his companions of that, and said, "I do not claim that I know the unseen, and I do not know it. But Allah has informed me of the hypocrite's words and of the place of my camel. It is in the ravine, its halter caught on a tree." They went running toward the ravine, and there it was, just as he had said; they brought it back, and that hypocrite believed.

When they reached Medina, they found that Rifa'ah ibn Zayd ibn al-Tabut had died that very day. He had been one of the great men of the Jews and a refuge for the hypocrites. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived at Medina, Zayd ibn Arqam said, "I sat in the house, because of the grief and shame I felt." So Allah the Exalted sent down Surat al-Munafiqun, confirming Zayd and denying Abdullah. When it was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took hold of Zayd's ear and said, "O Zayd, Allah has believed you and fulfilled [the truth of] your ear."

Abdullah ibn Ubayy was near Medina. When he wanted to enter it, his son Abdullah ibn Abdullah came and knelt his camel at the junction of the roads of Medina. When Abdullah ibn Ubayy came, [he said: "Behind you,"]^[Addition from "a" omitted; this is "ساقط من أ" (dropped from manuscript a).] he said, "What is wrong with you, woe to you?" He said, "No, by Allah, you shall never enter it except by the permission of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and today you will know who is the more honored and who is the more humble." Abdullah complained to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ of what his son had done, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent to him, "Let him go until he enters." He said, "As for the command of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, yes." So he entered, and he did not remain more than a few days before he fell ill and died.

They said: When the verse was revealed and the lie of Abdullah ibn Ubayy became clear, it was said to him, "O Abu Hubab, verily severe verses have been revealed about you, so go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he may ask forgiveness for you." He turned his head and said, "You ordered me to believe, and I believed; you ordered me to give the zakat of my wealth, and I have given it. There is nothing left but that I prostrate to Muhammad." So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿When it is said to them, "Come, so that the Messenger of Allah may ask forgiveness for you," they turn their heads﴾ [[Mentioned by Ibn Hisham in al-Sira: 3/302–305 (Dar al-Qalam edition), and al-Tabari: 28/115–117, and Ibn Kathir 4/370–371.]] ... the verse. And it was revealed: ﴿They are the ones who say, "Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse."﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 63, verses 7–8:

﴿They are the ones who say: "Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse"﴾ — yanfaddu (يَنْفَضُّوا) means they scatter, disperse. ﴿And to Allah belong the treasures of the heavens and the earth﴾ — so no one gives anything to anyone except by His permission, and none withholds it except by His will. ﴿But the hypocrites do not understand﴾ — that when He wills something, His command is only that He say to it "Be," and it is.

﴿They say: "If we return to Al-Madinah"﴾ — from the expedition of Banu al-Mustaliq — ﴿the most honorable will surely expel from it the most humble.﴾ ﴿And to Allah belongs honor, and to His Messenger and to the believers﴾ — so the honor of Allah is His subduing those who are beneath Him, the honor of His Messenger is the manifestation of his religion over all religions, and the honor of the believers is Allah's giving them victory over their enemies.

﴿But the hypocrites do not know﴾ — that is, had they known, they would not have uttered this statement.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 63, verse 9–10:

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿O you who have believed, let not your wealth and your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah﴾, i.e., let them not preoccupy you. The exegetes (mufassirun) said: it means the five prayers. A parallel to it is His saying: "Neither trade nor sale diverts them from the remembrance of Allah" [al-Nur: 37]. ﴿And whoever does that﴾, i.e., whoever is preoccupied by his wealth and his children from the remembrance of Allah, ﴿those are the losers﴾.

﴿And spend from what We have provided you﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: it means the zakat of wealth. ﴿Before death comes to one of you﴾, so that he asks for a return (raj'ah), ﴿and says, "My Lord, if only You would delay me"﴾, i.e., "Why did You not delay me? Grant me respite." It has also been said: "la" (in "lawla") is extra (silah), so the statement carries the sense of wishing, meaning: "If only You would delay me, ﴿for a short term, so I would give charity﴾, i.e., I would give charity and pay the zakat of my wealth, ﴿and be among the righteous﴾, i.e., among the believers."

A parallel to it is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And whoever was righteous among their fathers﴾ [al-Ra'd: 23] [Ghafir: 8]. This is the saying of Muqatil and a group. They said: the verse was revealed concerning the hypocrites. It has also been said that the verse was revealed concerning the believers.

What is meant by righteousness here is the Hajj. Al-Dahhak and 'Atiyyah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: No one dies who had wealth and did not pay its zakat, and was able to perform Hajj but did not perform it, except that he asks for a return at the time of death. Then he recited this verse, and said: ﴿and be among the righteous﴾. Abu 'Amr read "wa-akun" with a waw and with a fathah on the nun, as an answer to the wish (jawab al-tamanni) and in accordance with the wording "fa-assaddaq"; he said: the waw was omitted in the Mushaf for brevity.

The others read "wa-akun" with a jazm, coordinating it with his saying "fa-assaddaq" as if the fa' were not there, because if there were no fa', it would be jazm. The meaning is: "If You delay me, I will give charity and be [righteous]," and because it is written in the Mushaf without the waw.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 63, verse 11:

﴿And Allah will never delay a soul when its term has come; and Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾ Abu Bakr read "ya'malūna" (with the letter ya', meaning "they do"), while the others read it with the letter ta' ("ta'malūna", meaning "you do").
